title: Turn a context-window claim into a test matrix
description: Choose a behavior, sweep shape, maximum length, and distractor pressure. The grid shows which length-by-position claims your planned cases can actually support.

workloads.label: Single-fact retrieval
workloads.detail: Find one unique fact at a controlled position. Useful as a smoke test, not a full comprehension claim.
workloads.claim: This tests whether one known fact can be found under the selected placement and distractor conditions.

workloads.label: Multi-document reasoning
workloads.detail: Combine three facts split across documents and cite the evidence used for the final answer.
workloads.claim: This tests retrieval, evidence combination, and support completeness; it is harder than finding one unique string.

workloads.label: Global aggregation
workloads.detail: Count or summarize facts distributed through the whole input, so sampling only one region is insufficient.
workloads.claim: This tests whether the model uses the full context rather than locating one salient passage.

plans.label: One middle-position point
plans.detail: Fast and cheap, but it supports only one length-by-position slice.

plans.label: Depth sweep at one length
plans.detail: Moves the same evidence through the input to reveal position sensitivity.

plans.label: Length × depth grid
plans.detail: Tests every shown depth at each length through the selected maximum.

distractorLevels.label: Distinct filler
distractorLevels.detail: The evidence is lexically different from surrounding text.

distractorLevels.label: Plausible distractors
distractorLevels.detail: Nearby passages share entities and vocabulary but contain different facts.

distractorLevels.label: Conflicting evidence
distractorLevels.detail: Versioned or contradictory facts require source selection and calibrated abstention.
